name: Base32 Encoder / Decoder
description: Encode text to Base32 or decode Base32 back to text, per RFC 4648 — the encoding used for TOTP/2FA secret keys and other hand-typed identifiers.

faq.question: How is Base32 different from Base64?
faq.answer: Base32 uses a smaller, 32-character alphabet (A-Z and 2-7 — no lowercase, and it skips 0/1/8/9 to avoid confusion with O/I/B/g), so it's less compact than Base64 but far less error-prone to read or type by hand. That's why TOTP/2FA authenticator apps encode their secret keys in Base32: users occasionally need to manually retype one.

faq.question: Is decoding case-sensitive?
faq.answer: No — this decoder accepts both upper and lowercase input (Base32 output is conventionally uppercase, but many real-world tools and users produce or expect lowercase), and tolerates missing "=" padding at the end.
